kai (customer): Hey team — customer reports a large embeddings job failing with lots of 429s and some "dimension mismatch" errors intermittently. They say it started after switching to our new batcher. Sample error: `{"error": "rate_limited", "details": "burst_capacity_exceeded"}`

julia (support): Thanks @kai. Can you paste the exact request shape (batch size, embedding model name, dims) and any response headers like X-RateLimit-Remaining/X-RateLimit-Reset? Also which plan/account?

kai (customer): Using model: open-embed-1536, batch_size=256, concurrency=8 across 20 workers. Account: acct-xyz (pay-as-you-go). We do see headers: `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `x-ratelimit-limit: 1000/min`, `x-ratelimit-reset: 13`

mike (eng-sre): That looks like hitting a burst window. The new batcher may send many concurrent requests upfront. Recommend reducing per-worker concurrency to 2 and lowering batch_size to 64 while we investigate. Also add exponential backoff with jitter on 429s.

sophia (eng-ml): The "dimension mismatch" might be from mixed model variants — some requests went to an older quantized variant with 768 dims. Can you confirm all workers pin the same model version? If not, include `model_version` in requests or pin to `open-embed-1536:v3`.

kai (customer): Repro steps I used:
1) spawn 20 workers each doing:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{ "model": "open-embed-1536", "input": [..256 texts..] }
```
2) run simultaneously
3) observe 429s and occasional `dimension mismatch expected 1536 got 768`

julia (support): That's perfect. Can you also include one raw response body for a failed request and the `request-id` header so we can correlate in logs?

kai (customer): Pasted one failed response: `{"error":"rate_limited","message":"burst capacity exceeded","code":429}`. Request-ID: req_0b3a7

mike (eng-sre): Got it. I'm checking infra logs for req_0b3a7... rate-limiter-bot: any signaling?

rate-limiter-bot: ALERT: account acct-xyz exceeded burst quota threshold at 2026-03-15T14:02:11Z. Current concurrency=160, burst_limit=120

mike (eng-sre): Confirmed. We can do a temporary burst quota bump for acct-xyz to 200 for 30 minutes to help them finish. Sophia — can you confirm whether routing to mixed model variants could create the dim mismatch during fallback sequences?

sophia (eng-ml): Yes — fallback to older quantized variants would return 768-dim vectors. We'll add a guard so that fallback won't be used for embedding models (or convert/normalize dims on the client). For now ask customer to pin version.

julia (support): Action items for customer:
• Reduce concurrency to 2 per worker and batch_size to 64
• Add exponential backoff (base 500ms, max 10s) + full jitter on 429s
• Pin model_version to open-embed-1536:v3

mike (eng-sre): Internal actions:
• temporary burst bump applied (will notify) ✅
• rate-limiter team to add per-account pacing window tuning
• follow up in 2 hours

julia (support): @kai we've applied the temporary bump. Please retry the job with the mitigations and confirm. If you still see dimension mismatches include the first failing request-id.

kai (customer): Thanks — retrying now. Will report back in ~20m.

julia (support): thx :thumbsup:

mike (eng-sre): note for runbook: add doc snippet for embeddings bulk jobs: `set max_concurrency=4, batch_size<=128, backoff=exp+jitter, check x-ratelimit-* headers` — will add to KB.
